title: Canonical immersion stalk Frobenius comparison
statement: Let D be a finite-field datum, l a prime distinct from its characteristic, and Qbar an algebraic closure of the l-adic field, in a universe independent of that of D. For a locally closed immersion h0 between separated finite-type finite-field models, a closed source point z with closed image, an input constructible Weil sheaf F and any finite Weil presentation K of its canonical pullback, there is a finite Weil presentation Kprime of F and a compatible image residue embedding such that scalar-extended degree-zero stalks of K and Kprime are isomorphic, and this isomorphism intertwines their specified local geometric Frobenius operators. Both coefficient and scheme universes are arbitrary and independent. The exact objects, presentations and operator equation are the Lean statement. Uses [def-weil-constructible-heart; def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-punctual-weights; def-weil-closed-immersion; def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom; def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category; def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

proof.text: Descend the input sheaf with its Weil structure and inverse equations to one finite coefficient field. The canonical square zlFrobeniusSquare is the scalar inclusion of the two normalized integral pullback-composition comparisons, so the pulled-back finite Weil pair presents exactly the specified pullback.

proof.text: At compatible geometric lifts use the inverse pullback-composition stalk comparison. Residue fields of an immersion are isomorphic, so both return exponents agree. Induct on this exponent; associativity and point-transport naturality intertwine the three local Frobenius factors. Extend coefficients and take degree zero.

lean.statement:
theorem zlCanonicalImmersionStalkConjugacy (h₀ : W₀ ⟶ X₀) [IsImmersion h₀.left]
    (z : {z : W₀.left // z ∈ closedPoints W₀.left})
    (hx : h₀.left z.val ∈ closedPoints X₀.left)
    (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X₀ Qbar)
    (L : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Qbar)
    (K : sfWeilComplex D l hl W₀
      (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Qbar L))
    (hK : Nonempty (((zlWeilPull D l hl Qbar h₀).obj F).obj ≅
      sfWeilStageObject D l hl W₀ Qbar L K))
    (ι : W₀.left.residueField z.val →+* D.k)
    (hι : ι.comp (W₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap z.val) = algebraMap D.k₀ D.k) :
    ∃ (L' : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Qbar)
      (K' : sfWeilComplex D l hl X₀
        (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Qbar L')),
      Nonempty (F.obj ≅ sfWeilStageObject D l hl X₀ Qbar L' K') ∧
      ∃ (ι' : X₀.left.residueField (h₀.left z.val) →+* D.k)
        (hι' : ι'.comp (X₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap (h₀.left z.val)) =
          algebraMap D.k₀ D.k),
      ∃ e :
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (sfAdicCoefficientEmbedding.{u} l Qbar L)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.coefficientFdCohomology
            (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Qbar L) 0).obj
            (localPointComplex l _ D hl W₀ K (localClosedPoint D W₀ z ι hι))) ≅
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (sfAdicCoefficientEmbedding.{u} l Qbar L')).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.coefficientFdCohomology
            (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Qbar L') 0).obj
            (localPointComplex l _ D hl X₀ K'
              (localClosedPoint D X₀ ⟨h₀.left z.val, hx⟩ ι' hι'))),
        e.hom ≫ (ModuleCat.extendScalars (sfAdicCoefficientEmbedding.{u} l Qbar L')).map
            (localClosedFrobeniusCohomology l _ D hl X₀ K'
              ⟨h₀.left z.val, hx⟩ ι' hι' 0) =
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (sfAdicCoefficientEmbedding.{u} l Qbar L)).map
            (localClosedFrobeniusCohomology l _ D hl W₀ K z ι hι 0) ≫ e.hom
